::: {.lead}
In Lecture 11 you learned to edit: the basic tools of a video editor, cuts
and transitions, slow motion, colour and titles, and the sound and the
export. Today you edit a promotional clip of a game. There are no new
ideas: two short problems. Do each one alone. The results of the
activities are at the end of this worksheet.
:::

## Recall

- On the timeline, V2 covers V1; split, trim and ripple delete build the
  cut. A **cut on action** hides the cut inside a movement.
- Use cuts almost always; a **cross dissolve** says time passes; a **dip to
  black** ends a part.
- Titles stay inside the **title safe area** for at least 2 s; the voice
  stays above the music; export for the target.

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Recall"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="a wipe|the edge of the frame"}
Which cut hides the edit inside a movement?
:   a cut on action

Which transition says that time passes?
:   a cross dissolve

Where does all text belong?
:   inside the title safe area
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · Plan the promo

A **promo** of 30 seconds has five parts: the **hook** (0–3 s), **the
world**, the **gameplay beats** (short shots of 1–3 s), the **big
moment**, and the **logo with a call to action** (the last 5 s). Menus and
loading screens stay out. A **shot list** keeps only the shots that serve
a part: number, start time, content, length.

![A 30-second promo in five parts.](images/promo-structure.png){width=94%}

{{< sim file="sims/promo-builder.html" poster="sims/promo-builder.png" title="Promo Builder: 30 seconds of Rooftop Rescue" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 1 · Five parts and a shot list · 15 min"}
1. In **Promo Builder**, make all the checks green.
2. Write the shot list of your promo: the shots in order, each with its
   part and its length.

*Your product:* a shot list of 6–10 shots, 25–30 seconds in all.

::: {.check}
A good list starts with the wave hitting the roof (the hook, 3 s), shows
the flooded city (the world), three or four short level shots on the beat
(gameplay beats), Pasha safe on the roof (the big moment), and ends with
the logo and "Play free now" (5 s). No menu, no loading screen; 25–30 s in
all.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · The parts"}
Choose the part of the promo.

::: {.match extra="the credits|the menu"}
The wave hits the roof, and Nour jumps (0–3 s).
:   the hook

Three short level shots on the beat.
:   gameplay beats

"Play free now" with the logo.
:   the call to action

Which shots stay out of a promo?
:   menus and loading screens
:::
:::

## Activity 2 · Cut, review and export

Cut the promo with the **music first** on the timeline, and put the cuts
**on the beats**. Use cuts and cuts on action, and one dip to black before
the logo. Titles are **honest** (real features only) and inside the safe
area. Then watch the promo three times: as a player, with a checklist, and
on a phone.

![The review checklist.](images/promo-check.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 2 · The promo · 20 min"}
1. Cut your promo from the shot list: music, shots on the beats, one honest
   title, the logo and the call to action.
2. Watch it on a phone, fix one thing, and export `yourname-promo-v1.mp4`
   (H.264 in MP4).

*Your product:* one promo file of 25–30 seconds.

::: {.check}
A good promo starts with the hook, cuts on the beats, has one honest title
such as "Rescue cats in 30 levels" inside the safe area for at least 2 s,
a dip to black before the logo, and ends with the logo and the call to
action. Typical phone fixes: move a title away from the edge, or shorten a
6-second shot to about 3 s.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Cutting and review"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="the logo|“The best game ever!!!”"}
What goes on the timeline first?
:   the music

Which title is honest?
:   "Rescue cats in 30 levels"

The call to action is cut off on a phone. What do you do?
:   move it into the safe area

There is a 6-second shot in the middle. What do you do?
:   cut it to about 3 s
:::
:::

## Exercises

1. Name the five parts of a 30-second promo.
2. Why is a 5-second logo at the start a mistake?
3. Why does the music go on the timeline first?
4. Why must a promo title be honest?

## Answers to the exercises

::: {.answers}
1. The hook, the world, the gameplay beats, the big moment, the logo and the call to action.
2. Many viewers stop watching before the game appears.
3. The cuts can then go on its beats.
4. It must not promise features that the game does not have.
:::
